name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since Feb
summary: No US–Russia arms-control treaty since New START lapsed; a mid-Nov US–Russia–China communiqué set up a risk dialogue
state: New START expired without a replacement, and the US administration has raised the possibility of resuming nuclear explosive testing (Arms Control Association, 20 Nov). At a mid-November meeting in Shenzhen the US, Russian and Chinese leaders reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and agreed to a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks, which the association described as a starting point rather than a breakthrough. No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use in an active conflict was found to 23 Nov, so Watch holds on the arms-control lapse.
for_you: No direct effect on daily life. The lapse of treaty limits mainly removes inspections and data exchanges that let each side verify the other's forces.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired; no successor treaty)

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Opportunity for a course correction?

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
